notes:
Summary: Knotline runs customer support for a large US ecommerce marketplace. Primary goal is high-volume chat deflection to reduce Live Agent load during peaks (sales, holidays) while keeping handle-time and quality stable. Very cost-sensitive: currently spend ~$0.20 per conversation in prod and want that below $0.08 with equivalent QA scores.

Key pain: spikes of short chats (average 6-12 tokens per turn) — they pay for per-token hosted calls today (expensive). Trying to evaluate batching/caching and low-precision quantized models to reduce unit economics. SRE: 'If you can't guarantee tail latency during Black Friday-level spikes we won't go forward.'

User quotes / call snippets:
- "We need deflection to be reliable — not just on paper; routing must fallback gracefully or we swamp agents."
- "Our cost model collapses if the model doesn't batch effectively; we saw 2x token cost in holidays."

POC requirements (from Knotline):
- 1-week traffic replay using real chat traces (anonymized) at 2x baseline QPS
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-conversation, and deflection rate vs current heuristics
- Evaluate quantized 4-bit and 8-bit candidate profiles for their quality delta on intent detection and summarization
- Support tool-calling for order status + refunds (webhook integration + audit logs)

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support SSO (SAML) for internal console access
- Audit logging required for every tool call and model response that triggers an automated action
- KMS integration to manage keys for any cached data

Commercial notes:
- Interested in committed Dedicated pool if unit economics are proven — initial ask: price per hour for a 4-GPU reserved pool + burst pricing
- Open to hosted API + Optimize recommendations for first-phase if POC shows cost/latency wins

Sales diligence items:
- Provide sample cost model: cost per 1M messages at baseline and with caching/prefix KV reuse
- Provide quickstart for replay + ephemeral VPC connector doc (link above)
- Technical deep-dive scheduled with SRE on 2026-03-16 (prep: kernel selection, batching strategy, KV cache TTLs)
